# Tool reference

40 tools, all served by `darkroom mcp`. Every call is validated, journaled once (also on failure) and returned as JSON. Edit tools work on a virtual copy of the photo, never the original file, inside the guardrail limits (see `DESIGN.md`).

| Tool | Kind | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| [`get_app_status`](#get_app_status) | reads | Check whether Lightroom Classic and Photoshop are running and ready to be used. |
| [`get_capabilities`](#get_capabilities) | reads | Report the installed Lightroom Classic, plug-in and Photoshop versions, whether each is a version darkroom_ai was tested with, and which features are verified, untested, have a known issue or are unavailable. |
| [`run_selftest`](#run_selftest) | reads | Check, probe by probe, that the installed Lightroom Classic (and Photoshop, if it is already running) still behaves as darkroom_ai expects: versions, catalog read, every Develop key the tools use (drift check), metadata, presets, preview. |
| [`ensure_apps_running`](#ensure_apps_running) | reads | Start Lightroom Classic or Photoshop if it is not running, and wait until it answers. |
| [`get_photo_info`](#get_photo_info) | reads | Read facts about a photo and its current basic settings. |
| [`list_catalog_photos`](#list_catalog_photos) | reads | List photos in the open Lightroom catalog, one page at a time, with their ids and camera/lens/exposure facts. |
| [`catalog_summary`](#catalog_summary) | reads | Summarise the whole catalog: how many photos, and counts by camera, lens, ISO band, file format, star rating, capture year and folder. |
| [`scan_folder`](#scan_folder) | reads | Say what importing a folder would add to the catalog (new photos, already-present photos, unsupported files) without changing anything. |
| [`import_folder`](#import_folder) | writes | Add the photos in a folder to the catalog WITHOUT moving, copying or changing any file. |
| [`get_photo_metadata`](#get_photo_metadata) | reads | Read the camera, lens and exposure facts of a photo (make, model, lens, focal length, aperture, shutter speed, ISO, capture time, size, file type). |
| [`get_selected_photos`](#get_selected_photos) | reads | List the photo(s) selected in Lightroom Classic, with their catalog ids. |

| [`get_preview`](#get_preview) | reads | Render the photo as Lightroom shows it right now and return the picture itself, so you can look at it. |
| [`analyze_photo`](#analyze_photo) | reads | Export a small preview and measure it: tones, clipping, colour cast, faces if available. |
| [`analyze_batch`](#analyze_batch) | reads | Measure many photos in one call and return a few numbers per photo (tones, clipping, colour cast). |

### `get_app_status`

Reads only.

Check whether Lightroom Classic and Photoshop are running and ready to be used. Reads only: it never starts or closes anything. The connector block says which code this connector process runs and whether it is stale (older than the files on disk; restart it). States: ready; busy (a command runs or is stuck in Lightroom; the detail says how long); not_running; needs_user (running but not answering, e.g. a dialog is open; the next step says what to clear); not_installed; unknown.

No parameters.

### `get_capabilities`

Reads only.

Report the installed Lightroom Classic, plug-in and Photoshop versions, whether each is a version darkroom_ai was tested with, and which features are verified, untested, have a known issue or are unavailable. Reads only. Call it at the start of a session and before relying on an untested feature (for example RAW edits or people masks); tell the user about anything that is not 'verified' before you use it. An untested version is a warning, never a block.

No parameters.

### `run_selftest`

Reads only.

Check, probe by probe, that the installed Lightroom Classic (and Photoshop, if it is already running) still behaves as darkroom_ai expects: versions, catalog read, every Develop key the tools use (drift check), metadata, presets, preview. Run it after an Adobe update and report every probe. Reads only by default. With write=true it also makes ONE virtual copy in the test catalog, changes Exposure by +0.1 EV, reads it back and puts it back; that asks the user first. A failed probe means the matching tools may not work: say which.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `write` | boolean | no | `False` |  |

### `ensure_apps_running`

Reads only.

Start Lightroom Classic or Photoshop if it is not running, and wait until it answers. An app that is already running is never restarted. If it is running but not answering, you get state needs_user: tell the person what to clear, then call get_app_status until it says ready.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `app` | `lightroom` \| `photoshop` | yes |  |  |

### `get_photo_info`

Reads only.

Read facts about a photo and its current basic settings. Changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `list_catalog_photos`

Reads only.

List photos in the open Lightroom catalog, one page at a time, with their ids and camera/lens/exposure facts. Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `offset` | integer | no | `0` | How many photos to skip. min 0 |
| `limit` | integer | no | `25` | Most photos to return (1-100). min 1, max 100 |
| `path_contains` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos whose file path contains this text (e.g. a folder). |
| `include_virtual_copies` | boolean | no | `False` | Also list virtual copies (normally only the originals). |
| `min_rating` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos rated at least this (unrated counts as 0). |
| `max_rating` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos rated at most this (0 finds the unrated). |
| `flag` | `pick` \| `reject` \| `none` (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos with this flag. |
| `keyword` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos that have this keyword (any letter case). |
| `file_format` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos of this file format: RAW, DNG, JPG, TIFF, PSD or VIDEO. |
| `min_iso` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos at this ISO or higher. |
| `max_iso` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos at this ISO or lower. |
| `captured_from` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos captured on or after this date, written YYYY-MM-DD. |
| `captured_to` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos captured on or before this date, written YYYY-MM-DD. |

### `catalog_summary`

Reads only.

Summarise the whole catalog: how many photos, and counts by camera, lens, ISO band, file format, star rating, capture year and folder. Read only. Use it to understand a shoot or the library before editing, then list_catalog_photos to look at specific photos.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `max_photos` | integer | no | `2000` | min 50, max 10000 |
| `top` | integer | no | `10` | How many entries to list per group. min 3, max 30 |
| `path_contains` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only photos whose file path contains this text (a folder). |

### `scan_folder`

Reads only.

Say what importing a folder would add to the catalog (new photos, already-present photos, unsupported files) without changing anything. Always do this before import_folder.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string | yes |  | Absolute folder path, inside the allowed folder. min length 1 |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | `False` | Include sub-folders. |

### `import_folder`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Add the photos in a folder to the catalog WITHOUT moving, copying or changing any file. This is a bulk change: the person is asked for a go-ahead showing how many photos will be added, so call scan_folder first and tell them. Adds at most max_files new photos per call; call again for the rest. It cannot be undone with the undo tool (remove the photos in Lightroom if needed).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `folder` | string | yes |  | Absolute folder path, inside the allowed folder. min length 1 |
| `recursive` | boolean | no | `False` | Include sub-folders. |
| `max_files` | integer | no | `200` | min 1, max 500 |

Reads only.

### `analyze_photo`

Reads only.

Export a small preview and measure it: tones, clipping, colour cast, faces if available.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `analyze_batch`

Reads only.

Measure many photos in one call and return a few numbers per photo (tones, clipping, colour cast). Numbers only: no pictures, no faces, no verdicts. Use it to compare or group a large set cheaply before looking at individual photos. Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_ids` | list of string | yes |  | Catalog ids to measure (1-25); repeats are ignored. min items 1, max items 25 |
| `long_edge` | integer | no | `512` | Longest side of the measured preview in pixels (256-1024). Smaller is faster. min 256, max 1024 |
| `time_budget_s` | number | no | `90.0` | Stop starting new photos after this many seconds; the rest are listed in not_processed so you can call again with them. min 1.0, max 300.0 |

### `adjust_lighting`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change exposure and tone by the given amounts (relative to the current values). Values beyond the per-pass or total limits are clamped; the result lists what was applied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `exposure` | number (may be null) | no | `None` | Change in EV; positive brightens, negative darkens. |
| `contrast` | number (may be null) | no | `None` | Change on the -100..100 scale. |
| `highlights` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `shadows` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `whites` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `blacks` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `allow_beyond_total` | boolean | no | `False` | Go beyond the total limit for this photo. Needs the user's confirmation. |

### `adjust_white_balance`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change white balance by the given amounts. JPG/TIFF: both values are on Lightroom's relative -100..100 scale (positive temperature = warmer, positive tint = more magenta). RAW: temperature is a change in Kelvin. Values beyond the per-pass or total limits are clamped; the result lists what was applied.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `temperature` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `tint` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `allow_beyond_total` | boolean | no | `False` | Go beyond the total limit for this photo. Needs the user's confirmation. |

### `list_develop_parameters`

Reads only.

List the Lightroom develop parameters you can read and set with get_develop_parameters and set_develop_parameters (name, panel, allowed range). Changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `panel` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Panel: basic, detail, lens, geometry, effects, color_grading, calibration. |

### `get_develop_parameters`

Reads only.

Read the current value of develop settings of a photo (or its working copy). Give the exact Lightroom setting names, e.g. "Clarity2012"; leave names empty for all listed parameters. Any Lightroom develop setting name can be read, not only the listed ones: for example the text settings in list_develop_parameters (readable_text_settings), such as LensProfileName, show whether Lightroom found a lens profile.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `names` | list of string | no |  | max items 80 |

### `set_develop_parameters`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change listed develop parameters of a photo's virtual copy. Each value is the CHANGE to apply (positive or negative), not the final value; it is limited to the parameter's range and to a per-call amount. The original is never touched. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `changes` | object | yes |  |  |

### `list_masks`

Reads only.

List the masks (local adjustments) on a photo or its working copy: how many, their names and the local adjustment values they carry. Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `create_mask`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Create a mask on the photo's virtual copy; it starts with no adjustments (use set_mask_adjustments next). Positions are fractions of the picture as shown in Lightroom: x 0 = left, 1 = right; y 0 = top, 1 = bottom (the same fractions as in get_preview). - mask_type 'gradient': give start and end. The effect is full at start and fades to nothing at end. - mask_type 'radialGradient': give center, radius_x, radius_y (fractions of the width and height; the ellipse spans center +- radius), optional feather (0-100, default 50) and angle (degrees, default 0). The effect is inside the ellipse; use invert_mask for outside. - mask_type 'rangeMask' with subtype 'luminance': give luminance_range = four brightness values 0-1 in rising order (a, b, c, d): the mask ramps in from a to b, is full from b to c and ramps out from c to d (0, 0, 1, 1 = the whole tonal range). - mask_type 'aiSelection' with subtype subject, sky, background, objects or landscape. Lightroom switches to Develop while this runs; the person should not click in Lightroom meanwhile. - mask_type 'aiSelection' with subtype 'people': Lightroom only makes it after a person is chosen and 'Create Mask' is pressed in its panel, so the tool asks the person to do that, then waits up to a minute for the mask and checks it. - rangeMask color or depth cannot be created automatically yet. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `mask_type` | `aiSelection` \| `rangeMask` \| `gradient` \| `radialGradient` | yes |  |  |
| `subtype` | string (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `start` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `end` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `center` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `radius_x` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `radius_y` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `feather` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `angle` | number (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `luminance_range` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` |  |

### `inspect_masks`

Reads only.

Show the masks of a photo's working copy as Lightroom reports them, including each mask's id (needed by set_mask_adjustments, invert_mask and delete_mask). Lightroom switches to the Develop module while this runs. Changes nothing in the picture.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |

### `set_mask_adjustments`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Change local adjustments inside ONE mask, so only the masked area changes. Each value is the CHANGE to apply (positive or negative), not the final value, limited to the parameter's range and to a per-call amount (exposure 1.5 EV; others a quarter of their range). Names: see LOCAL_PARAMETERS in the error text if you use a wrong one. mask_id comes from create_mask or inspect_masks; leave it out to use the mask currently selected in Lightroom. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `mask_id` | string (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `changes` | object | yes |  |  |

### `invert_mask`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Invert one mask so it covers everything it did not (for example: select the subject, then invert to adjust the background). Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `mask_id` | string | yes |  | From create_mask or inspect_masks. min length 1 |

### `delete_mask`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Delete one mask from the working copy (the original photo is never touched). Undo with the undo tool restores it.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `mask_id` | string | yes |  | From create_mask or inspect_masks. min length 1 |

### `get_tone_curve`

Reads only.

Read a photo's tone curve as points on a 0-255 scale. Changes nothing. channel "rgb" is the combined curve; "red", "green" and "blue" are the colour curves. A straight line from (0,0) to (255,255) means no curve.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `channel` | `rgb` \| `red` \| `green` \| `blue` | no | `rgb` |  |

### `adjust_tone_curve`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Set a tone curve on the photo's working copy (a virtual copy; never the original). Give the whole curve as points on a 0-255 scale, from x=0 to x=255 with x increasing (2 to 16 points). Read the current curve first with get_tone_curve and change it a little: each output is limited to a small step from the current curve and to a bounded distance from a straight line, and outputs never fall below the point before. Anything limited is reported in `note`. channel "rgb" is the combined curve; "red", "green", "blue" are the colour curves. Undo with the ordinary undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `channel` | `rgb` \| `red` \| `green` \| `blue` | no | `rgb` |  |
| `points` | list of any | yes |  | min items 2, max items 16 |

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Cut out the subject and put it on a new background. Give `color` or `image`, not both.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
| `color` | list of any (may be null) | no | `None` | Background colour as red, green, blue (0-255). |
| `image` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | File NAME of a picture in the configured backgrounds folder (no path). |

### `undo`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Take back darkroom_ai's edits made in THIS session: the last one, or all of them. Edits from earlier sessions cannot be taken back with this tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `scope` | `last` \| `all` | no | `last` |  |

### `get_library_state`

Reads only.

Read a photo's star rating, pick/reject flag and keywords. Changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |

### `set_library_state`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Set a virtual copy's star rating, pick/reject flag and keywords (catalog data only). rating is 0-5 (0 clears the rating); flag is "pick", "reject" or "none"; add_keywords and remove_keywords are plain names (an existing keyword of that name is reused, a new one is created at the top level of the keyword list). Only virtual copies are changed, never a master photo. The change is read back from Lightroom and can be taken back with undo_library_change.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `rating` | integer (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `flag` | `pick` \| `reject` \| `none` (may be null) | no | `None` |  |
| `add_keywords` | list of string | no |  | max items 20 |
| `remove_keywords` | list of string | no |  | max items 20 |

### `undo_library_change`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Take back darkroom_ai's library changes (rating, flag, keywords) made in THIS session. scope "last" takes back the most recent one; "all" takes back all of them on this photo. Keywords that were created are left in Lightroom's keyword list (only removed from the photo).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `scope` | `last` \| `all` | no | `last` |  |

### `batch_set_library_state`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Set rating, pick/reject flag and keywords on several virtual copies in one batch (up to 25). Each item names a photo and its values (same rules as set_library_state: virtual copies only, never a master). Everything is checked first; if any item is not allowed nothing runs. A batch of more than 5 photos needs the person's go-ahead, which this tool asks for itself. The run stops at the first failure and lists what was done, failed and not run. Use dry_run to see the plan without changing anything. Take a whole batch back with undo_batch.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of any | yes |  | min items 1, max items 25 |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `False` | Only check and show the plan; change nothing. |

### `batch_set_develop_parameters`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Edit several photos in one batch (up to 10), each with its own values, on virtual copies. Each item gives changes for exposure and tone, white balance and/or other develop settings; every value goes through the same limits as adjust_lighting, adjust_white_balance and set_develop_parameters, and a master gets one new working copy (the plan says how many will be created). Always needs the person's go-ahead, which this tool asks for itself. Everything is checked first; the run stops at the first failure and lists what was done, failed and not run. Use dry_run to see the plan without changing anything. Take a whole batch back with undo_batch (settings are restored; created copies stay in the catalog).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | list of any | yes |  | min items 1, max items 25 |
| `dry_run` | boolean | no | `False` | Only check and show the plan; change nothing. |

### `undo_batch`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Take back every change of one batch made in THIS session, by its batch_id. Restores settings and library fields from the journal and reads them back. Virtual copies a batch created are not deleted (deleting is never done). Changes made to the same photos after the batch are not separated out: the oldest recorded values are put back.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `batch_id` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |

### `list_presets`

Reads only.

List Lightroom's develop presets (name and folder). Reads only; changes nothing.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `contains` | string (may be null) | no | `None` | Only presets whose name or folder contains this text. |
| `limit` | integer | no | `100` | Most presets to return. min 1, max 500 |

### `apply_preset`

**Writes** (changes the catalog or a photo's settings).

Apply one of Lightroom's develop presets (a saved look) to the photo's virtual copy, by its exact name from list_presets. The result lists every setting the preset changed, with before and after, so look at get_preview and judge it. A preset that moves exposure far from the original, or changes the crop or process version, is taken back automatically. Undo with the undo tool.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `photo_id` | string | yes |  | Catalog id of the photo or its working copy. min length 1 |
| `preset_name` | string | yes |  | min length 1 |
